copy.aboutLead: A clearer path through rare disease research.
copy.aboutBody: Zebratlas connects genes, conditions, studies, communities and researchers through their source evidence. Follow a connection, check what supports it and start your next conversation.
copy.aboutEvidence: Every connection has a source. Inferred relationships and gaps stay visible. A search can reveal research possibilities; fit, access and participation must be confirmed with the responsible team.

aboutData.edgeScope: Relationship counts cover the connected research graph. Clinical associations are listed separately and may overlap. Recorded checksums have not been reverified by this view.

briefTasks.title: Request a model, sample or dataset
briefTasks.ask: Can you confirm this asset's suitability, current stock and access terms for this research?
questions: What is the native asset ID/version, genotype, tissue or model system?
Which measured evidence supports fit for this disease, gene and variant? What mismatch and control/QC would matter?
Does dated custodian evidence confirm this particular asset can be requested or downloaded? Is stock available now?
Who holds it, which official route handles requests, and what permitted uses, associated-data rights or transfer terms apply? Owner interest remains unconfirmed.

briefTasks.title: Ask about a therapy programme
briefTasks.ask: Can your programme team assess feasibility for this mechanism and population?
questions: What product/modality, developer, exact population and mechanism does the programme cover?
What is the source-dated development stage? Separate a proposed target, measured rescue and clinical outcomes.
What delivery, variant or population mismatch limits transfer? Which reference or use rights still need confirmation?
Who is the responsible developer, and which official programme route can review feasibility?

briefTasks.title: Write to a parent group
briefTasks.ask: Does your group support this diagnosis, and what is the first step to contact you?
questions: Does the group's own scope explicitly name this diagnosis, rather than only mentioning a gene?
Which official public contact channel is current?
What support, introductory conversation or registry information could we ask about? Add personal details only if you choose.

briefTasks.title: Ask about a study or site
briefTasks.ask: Can the study team confirm site recruitment, eligibility criteria and participation burden?
questions: What is the study/registry native ID, study type and exact or broader population scope?
What dated evidence describes overall recruitment and the specific site's location/status? Unknown site status does not mean recruiting.
Which official coordinator route handles inquiries? What criteria, visits, travel, follow-up and burden should be checked?
Individual eligibility remains a separate decision for the study team.

briefTasks.title: Review a cohort component
briefTasks.ask: Can the protocol owner review reuse of this component, including fit, burden and permissions?
questions: Which identifiable protocol, measure, dictionary or natural-history component is proposed, and what is its scientific purpose?
Is this a contact registry or longitudinal observation? What population differences limit reuse?
What burden, follow-up, missing-data handling and measurement compatibility need review?
Who owns the component, what access/use rights and current status are documented, and which official review route applies? Approval is not inherited.

briefTasks.title: Plan a mechanism or assay question
briefTasks.ask: Which assay and control would resolve the mechanism question for the supplied gene or variant?
questions: What disease/gene/allele context was actually provided? Unknown variant effects remain unknown.
What was measured, in which system, and what competing interpretation or limitation applies? Pathogenicity alone is not a functional result.
Which assay, comparator and control could distinguish the competing interpretations?
Who is qualified to review it, and what official institutional channel can be used?

briefTasks.title: Approach a bridging researcher
briefTasks.ask: Would the researcher review what could transfer between these two communities?
questions: Is this person's identity disambiguated, with evidence of work in each of two named communities?
Which papers, grants or studies support the link? What could transfer, and what scientific limitation remains?
Is the institution/contact route current and official? Shared names or symptoms do not establish identity or mechanism.

briefTasks.title: Check a funding route
briefTasks.ask: Can the programme office confirm a current funding route, its deadline and applicant requirements?
questions: What is the native call/award ID, funder, scope and official URL?
Is this a current call with dated open status/deadline, or a historical award used only as precedent?
What applicant, geographic and institutional constraints apply?
Which official programme-office route can confirm current availability and the next application step?

briefTasks.title: Locate lawful full text
briefTasks.ask: Where can I access the legal full text, and which version is available?
questions: What is the persistent paper ID and relevant mechanism/asset question, including its limitation?
Does an opened official publisher/repository URL supply full text? A DOI landing page or abstract alone is insufficient.
What version is available and under which access/license conditions? An unverified copy does not establish lawful access.

briefTasks.title: Compare related communities
briefTasks.ask: Which shared mechanism supports this connection, and which difference limits it?
questions: Which community has source-supported relevance, exact scope and an official route?
Which links are observed, inferred or hypotheses? Do not transfer one variant's effect to an entire gene.
Which sourced counterexample or limitation changes the interpretation? What mechanism difference should be tested?

briefTasks.title: Prepare a shared research proposal
briefTasks.ask: Can the partner review this proposed hypothesis and agree on a deciding experiment?
questions: Who is the real recipient, and which official route is appropriate?
Which three distinct, supported factual reasons justify the collaboration? Fewer than three supported reasons leaves this criterion unresolved.
What falsifiable shared question is proposed, and what component could be reused? Unsupported premises must be labelled hypotheses.
What contrary evidence/limitation, deciding experiment and reviewer are needed?

briefTasks.title: Document gaps and a next step
briefTasks.ask: Which specific source or community could help resolve this documented gap?
questions: Which exact groups and studies were found? If none, this means no record found within the documented search, not that none exists.
For groups and studies separately, which sources, query/aliases/languages, dates, pages and blocked requests were actually checked? Unrecorded fields remain unknown.
Which related route is source-supported, or was no related route found? Why do near misses not qualify?
Which specialist, registry or community-building question could close the gap, and which official route can receive it?

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: You can use Zebratlas without an account.
privacy.profiles: Public research profiles show names, affiliations and source links from public research records. They do not include private contact details. If an entry concerns you, you can ask us to remove it, correct it or review your objection.

sections.title: Accounts and saved items
sections.body: We store your email address, optional display name, secured password and what you choose to save. A session cookie keeps you signed in. You can export your account data or delete your account from Account.

sections.title: Requests and contributions
sections.body: Your email address and privacy request go to a private review queue. They are not published. Accepted data contributions are shown with their source, without your contact details.

sections.title: Documents, searches and models
sections.body: Search text and document content are sent in request bodies, not page links. The processor notice beside the search identifies the model service before you submit. Review that notice before sending personal information. We do not send messages on your behalf.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can request access, correction, deletion or object to processing, and complain to a data protection authority. Contact the controller below or use the private request form.

imprint.lead: Information according to § 5 DDG (German Digital Services Act).
imprint.private: Zebratlas is a private project by Johannes Mitschunas, not a service of Friedrich Schiller University Jena.

privacy.requestLead: If a public entry concerns you or your organisation, ask us to remove or correct it, or object to its processing. You do not need an account.
privacy.handling: Your request is reviewed privately. We may ask for proportionate proof that you are the affected person or represent the organisation. We aim to decide within 30 days.
privacy.hint: Give the entry link, name, ORCID or a short description. Include only what we need to locate and review it.
privacy.error: The request could not be sent. Check your email and keep the description under 2,000 bytes, or contact the controller.
privacy.receivedBody: Your request is in the private review queue. Keep this reference. Receipt does not mean the request has been approved.
